compiled_state.title: As a DSO plugin maintainer, I want a three-variant regression fixture family run through brainstorm and preplanning with a test asserting each fixture fires a distinct named gate, so that the three enforcement gates stay wired and cannot silently regress.
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description
**What**: Create the regression fixture family at plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/cross-skill-integration/ with exactly three variants, each mapped one-to-one onto a distinct named gate: tag-fork/ (producer emits copy-story, consumer detects copy:needed — the f360-3a5b shape; fires the drift gate, check (a)), contract-mismatch/ (a contract-doc-bearing variant: ships plugins/dso/docs/contracts/<canonical_name>.md whose canonical_surface mismatches the producer surface / consumer detection; fires the canonical-anchor gate, check (b)), and zero-declaration/ (producer touches tag-emit patterns but declares zero signals; fires the heuristic-undeclared-signal post-pass, sc-4). The prior surface-typo-coherence variant is repurposed into contract-mismatch because the typo variant shipped no contract doc and so could never reach check (b), leaving the canonical-anchor gate exercised by no fixture. Each variant fed through /dso:brainstorm -> /dso:preplanning independently fires exactly one of the three distinct gate identifiers. A dedicated regression test asserts the three pairings and fails on any collision or on the canonical-anchor gate going unfired.
**Why**: Without a regression family, the three gates from draft-3/draft-4/draft-5 can silently rot, and the canonical-anchor gate in particular was reachable by no fixture.
**Scope**:
- IN: exactly three fixture variants (tag-fork, contract-mismatch, zero-declaration) mapped one-to-one onto the three named gates; the contract doc shipped by the contract-mismatch variant; feeding each through brainstorm -> preplanning; the regression test asserting three distinct gate identifiers and failing on collision or on canonical-anchor going unfired.
- OUT: adding a fourth variant (the epic constrains the family to exactly three); the gates themselves (draft-3/draft-4/draft-5); the gate identifier strings (draft-3 owns them).

## Done Definitions

- The directory plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/cross-skill-integration/ contains exactly three variant subdirectories tag-fork, contract-mismatch, and zero-declaration ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The tag-fork variant fed through /dso:brainstorm then /dso:preplanning fires the drift gate identifier ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The contract-mismatch variant ships a contract doc whose canonical_surface mismatches its producer surface and consumer detection, and fed through brainstorm then preplanning it fires the canonical-anchor gate identifier ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The zero-declaration variant fed through brainstorm then preplanning fires the heuristic-undeclared-signal post-pass gate identifier ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The regression test asserts three distinct gate identifiers across the three fixtures and fails if any two fixtures fire the same gate or if the canonical-anchor gate is fired by none ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the three one-to-one fixture-gate assertions and the collision-detection assertion, run green via test-batched.sh ← Satisfies: sc-5

## Considerations

- [Distinct-gates] Each fixture maps one-to-one onto exactly one named gate: tag-fork -> drift, contract-mismatch -> canonical-anchor, zero-declaration -> heuristic-undeclared-signal. The regression test fails on any collision and on the canonical-anchor gate being fired by no fixture.
- [Variant-repurpose] The prior surface-typo-coherence variant is renamed and repurposed into contract-mismatch: it now ships a contract doc whose canonical_surface diverges from the producer surface and consumer detection, so check (b) is reachable. The typo variant could never reach check (b) because it shipped no contract doc (red-team / blue-team finding). The family stays at exactly three variants.
- [Coupling] This story depends on draft-3 (drift and canonical-anchor gate identifiers), draft-4 (fan-in gate), and draft-5 (heuristic-undeclared-signal post-pass) existing; the gate identifier strings asserted here are the contract draft-3 emits, so this test breaks if draft-3 renames an identifier.
- [Stability] Keep exactly three variants now per the epic's exactly-three constraint; the family is designed to grow in future post-mortems, not in this story.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
